findings.heading: Casos Linelist em semanas / Linelist cases into weeks
findings.proposition: The English instructs the reader to call floor_date() with unit = "week"; the Portuguese instructs unit = "semana", which is not the value used in the code chunk immediately below (unit = "week") and is not a unit lubridate accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader who follows the prose instead of copying the chunk writes floor_date(date_onset, unit = "semana") and gets an error from lubridate, with no indication that the instruction, not their data, is wrong.

findings.heading: Casos da Linelist em meses / Linelist cases into months
findings.proposition: The English gives the floor_date() argument as unit = "months"; the Portuguese gives unit = "meses", which contradicts the code chunk below it (unit = "months") and is not a unit lubridate accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader aggregating cases into months writes unit = "meses" and the call fails, so the monthly aggregation cannot be reproduced from the prose.

findings.heading: Casos da Linelist em meses / Linelist cases into months
findings.proposition: The English says the complete() step also uses by = "months"; the Portuguese says by = "meses", which contradicts the code chunk below it (by="month") and is not a value seq.Date() accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader filling in missing months writes by = "meses" inside seq.Date() and the sequence call errors, so the gap-filling step described in the section cannot be run.

findings.heading: Agrupoando por data / Grouping by date
findings.proposition: The English tells the reader to supply fill = list(n = 0) to complete(); the Portuguese tells the reader to supply fill = lista(n = 0), translating the base R function list() into Portuguese, so the named argument no longer names an existing R function.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader who types fill = lista(n = 0) gets 'could not find function "lista"', and the stated purpose of the argument (setting filled-in rows to 0 instead of NA) is never achieved.

findings.heading: Adicionar totais / Add totals
findings.proposition: The English names the janitor function adorn_percentages(); the Portuguese names adorn_percentagens(), which is not a janitor function and contradicts the code chunk immediately below, which calls adorn_percentages().
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader searching help for adorn_percentagens() or typing it into a pipeline finds no such function, and may conclude the janitor percentage helper does not exist.
